tools.name: send_plan_change_notice
tools.description: Switches a subscription to a new plan in the subscriptions database, records the change in the plan history, and emails the customer a confirmation of the new plan.

params.name: subscription_id
params.description: ID of the subscription to change

params.name: new_plan_code
params.description: Code of the plan to switch to

params.name: customer_email
params.description: Email address to send the confirmation to

tools.code:
import smtplib
import sqlite3
from contextlib import closing
from datetime import datetime, timezone
from email.message import EmailMessage

from mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP

mcp = FastMCP("subscriptions")

DB_PATH = "subscriptions.db"
SMTP_HOST = "smtp.internal.example.com"
SMTP_PORT = 587
SENDER = "billing@example.com"


@mcp.tool()
def send_plan_change_notice(subscription_id: str, new_plan_code: str, customer_email: str) -> dict:
    now = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    with closing(sqlite3.connect(DB_PATH)) as conn:
        with conn:
            plan = conn.execute(
                "SELECT name, price_cents FROM plans WHERE code = ?", (new_plan_code,)
            ).fetchone()
            if plan is None:
                return {"ok": False, "error": f"Unknown plan {new_plan_code}"}
            current = conn.execute(
                "SELECT plan_code FROM subscriptions WHERE id = ?", (subscription_id,)
            ).fetchone()
            if current is None:
                return {"ok": False, "error": f"Unknown subscription {subscription_id}"}
            conn.execute(
                "UPDATE subscriptions SET plan_code = ?, updated_at = ? WHERE id = ?",
                (new_plan_code, now, subscription_id),
            )
            conn.execute(
                "INSERT INTO plan_history (subscription_id, old_plan, new_plan, changed_at) "
                "VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
                (subscription_id, current[0], new_plan_code, now),
            )

    msg = EmailMessage()
    msg["From"] = SENDER
    msg["To"] = customer_email
    msg["Subject"] = "Your subscription plan has changed"
    msg.set_content(
        f"Your subscription {subscription_id} is now on the {plan[0]} plan "
        f"at ${plan[1] / 100:.2f} per billing period."
    )
    with smtplib.SMTP(SMTP_HOST, SMTP_PORT) as server:
        server.starttls()
        server.send_message(msg)

    return {"ok": True, "subscription_id": subscription_id, "plan": new_plan_code}

tools.name: run_renewal_batch_job
tools.description: Runs the renewal processing script for subscriptions renewing on a given date and returns its exit status and output summary.

params.name: dry_run
params.description: Whether to run the job without applying renewals

params.name: timeout_seconds
params.description: Maximum seconds to let the job run

tools.code:
import re
import subprocess
import time

SCRIPT_PATH = "/opt/billing/scripts/process_renewals.py"


def run_renewal_batch_job(renewal_date: str, dry_run: bool = True, timeout_seconds: int = 300) -> dict:
    result = {
        "renewal_date": renewal_date,
        "dry_run": dry_run,
        "success": False,
        "exit_code": None,
        "stdout_tail": [],
        "stderr_tail": [],
        "duration_seconds": None,
        "error": None,
    }

    if not re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}", renewal_date):
        result["error"] = "renewal_date must be YYYY-MM-DD"
        return result

    cmd = ["python3", SCRIPT_PATH, "--date", renewal_date]
    if dry_run:
        cmd.append("--dry-run")

    started = time.monotonic()
    try:
        proc = subprocess.run(
            cmd,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=timeout_seconds,
            check=False,
        )
    except subprocess.TimeoutExpired:
        result["error"] = f"Job timed out after {timeout_seconds} seconds"
        result["duration_seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 2)
        return result
    except OSError as exc:
        result["error"] = str(exc)
        return result

    result["duration_seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 2)
    result["exit_code"] = proc.returncode
    result["stdout_tail"] = proc.stdout.strip().splitlines()[-10:]
    result["stderr_tail"] = proc.stderr.strip().splitlines()[-10:]
    result["success"] = proc.returncode == 0
    if not result["success"]:
        result["error"] = "Renewal job exited with a non-zero status"
    return result

tools.name: charge_overage_fees
tools.description: Charges the customer's saved payment method for usage overage on a subscription and runs the invoice finalization script for that charge.

params.name: overage_units
params.description: Number of units used beyond the plan allowance

tools.code:
import subprocess

import stripe
from agents import function_tool as tool

UNIT_PRICE_CENTS = 25


def _finalize_invoice(payment_intent_id: str) -> int:
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["/opt/billing/bin/finalize_invoice.sh", payment_intent_id],
        capture_output=True,
        check=False,
    )
    return proc.returncode


@tool
def charge_overage_fees(customer_id: str, overage_units: int) -> str:
    customer = stripe.Customer.retrieve(customer_id)
    intent = stripe.PaymentIntent.create(
        amount=overage_units * UNIT_PRICE_CENTS,
        currency="usd",
        customer=customer_id,
        payment_method=customer.invoice_settings.default_payment_method,
        off_session=True,
        confirm=True,
    )
    code = _finalize_invoice(intent.id)
    return f"Charged {intent.amount} cents ({intent.status}); finalize exit {code}"
